newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIANS PICK GILLESPIE FOR THIRD TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIANS PICK GILLESPIE FOR THIRD TEST.

text.p: New South Wales pace bowler Jason Gillespie has proved his fitness and won a return to the Australian team for the third test against England starting at Old Trafford on Thursday.
Gillespie missed the second test at Lord's after suffering a hamstring injury in the first match of the series at Edgbaston but he now replaces Mike Kasprowicz of Queensland.

Taking five wickets for 33 in the victory over Hampshire this week confirmed his place, though captain Mark Taylor said: "It was one of the toughest selection decisions I've had to make as a tour selector because 'Kaspro' has bowled very well.
"But it's not just about this tour -- Jason was our leading wicket-taker in South Africa so his credentials are very good."
The Australian side is otherwise unchanged from Lord's as they seek the win that would level the series.
England's captain Michael Atherton regards it as a pivotal match. "We're halfway through the series and if we win and go two up that puts us in a very strong position," he said.
Atherton believes that his team can contribute further to an unexpectedly good sporting year for England.

A good showing in tennis at Wimbledon, the European Cup athletics and soccer's Tournoi de France have followed England's dramatic victory in the first test, which fuelled hopes of regaining the Ashes for the first time since 1985.
"It's been a positive summer for British sport," Atherton said. "We've played our part and I hope we can continue to do so."
England's team will not be named until the morning of the match, after the pitch at Atherton's home ground has been studied.
Mike Smith of Gloucestershire remains favourite for the one place that three bowlers seem to be disputing.
History would be made if he misses out to Kent's Dean Headley, whose father Ron and grandfather George both played test cricket -- albeit for the West Indies.
The forecast is for showers on the first day, a slight improvement on Friday and dry weather on Saturday and Sunday.
England (probable)- Michael Atherton (captain), Mark Butcher, Alec Stewart, Nasser Hussain, Graham Thorpe, John Crawley, Mark Ealham, Robert Croft, Darren Gough, Andy Caddick, Mike Smith.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Elliott, Greg Blewett, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Mark Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath.
